source: Ge & Parikh (2021) Visual Conceptual Blending with Large-scale Language and Vision Models
finding: Early test of whether language models can pick a blend partner and a hinge property. Masked-LM prompts ('the moon is like a [MASK]', then 'the ghost has the property of [MASK]') beat the ConceptNet knowledge base at associating concepts.
numbers: Simile test set: 66,442 property-object pairs. Precision of the true property in the top 10/100/1000 candidates. Best row: 2.59 / 24.84 / 66.38. Lowest row (ConceptNet): 1.12 / 2.70 / 5.90. Larger LMs scored higher. Column labels in the extracted table were garbled, so the model-to-row mapping is approximate.
limits: Masked-LM era (ELMo, BERT, GPT-1). Tests property retrieval, not emergent structure. Simile data is noisy.
agent_relevance: Two-step 'pick partner, then pick hinge property' is a cheap blend generator. A shape-guided prompt (find a property of A, then ask which B shares it) gave visually relevant partners.

source: Ge & Parikh (2021) Visual Conceptual Blending with Large-scale Language and Vision Models
finding: Two-phase pipeline: reasoning phase (LM picks object and property, writes a one-line blend like 'a moon that is sliced like an orange'), generation phase (CLIP-guided BigGAN or SIREN). Human rating on AMT used questions mapped to Fauconnier-Turner optimality principles (unpacking, integration, general quality).
numbers: 20 blend descriptions x 6 questions x 9 raters each. BigSleep and DeepDaze (CLIP-based) significantly beat DF-GAN; BigSleep preferred over DeepDaze. Exact percentages only in a figure.
limits: Only 20 descriptions, 9 raters each. Raters judged the image, so the language step and image step are confounded. No human-made blend baseline.
agent_relevance: Shows how to turn optimality principles into rater questions. Good template for a rubric that checks 'both inputs recognisable' and 'integrated'.

source: Song et al. (2025) Is a Peeled Apple Still Red? Evaluating LLMs' Ability for Conceptual Combination with Property Type (CCPT)
finding: New benchmark for conceptual combination (CCPT, 12,315 triplets of noun phrase, property, property type: component, emergent, canceled). LLMs, including o1 and GPT-4o, find emergent properties harder to generate than canceled ones. Writing a noun phrase that yields a given emergent property is harder still.
numbers: Noun-phrase completion: emergent score E is 27 or lower for all baseline LLMs; humans 38.0, gold 59.9. Property induction, emergent: humans E 49.2; canceled C 58.6 (LLM-judge scale). GPT-4o's generated properties are 12.3 points more related to a single component than gold is, i.e. models reuse an inherited property instead of an emergent one.
limits: Judge is GPT-4o. Human check was an N=30 sub-sample. Annotators were MTurk (commonsense of one demographic). The finding is about emergence, the heart of Fauconnier-Turner ('structure in neither input').
agent_relevance: Models default to inherited properties. A blend step should test 'does the property hold for neither input alone?' with a separate call or code, not trust the first draft.
quote: LLMs, including OpenAI's o1, struggle to generate noun phrases which possess given emergent properties.

source: Song et al. (2025) Is a Peeled Apple Still Red? Evaluating LLMs' Ability for Conceptual Combination with Property Type (CCPT)
finding: Property-type prediction: GPT-4o can say whether a noun phrase has a property but is weak at saying why (inherited, emergent, canceled).
numbers: GPT-4o yes/no property check 82.6% accuracy. Type prediction correct only 56.4% vs human 81% (human majority vote: emergent 87%, component 79%, canceled 76%). 1000 instances, 250 per type.
limits: One model tested on this task. Human accuracy from a separate MTurk check.
agent_relevance: Models over-credit 'emergent'. Do not let the agent label its own blend emergent without a check against both inputs.

source: Song et al. (2025) Is a Peeled Apple Still Red? Evaluating LLMs' Ability for Conceptual Combination with Property Type (CCPT)
finding: Scaffold that helped: a 'spread activation' prompt (iteratively retrieve related concepts from the LLM and ConceptNet, filter distractors, then answer) improved all three generative tasks over base and chain-of-thought. More iterations helped slowly; removing the filter hurt.
numbers: GPT-4o, iteration 1 to 5: property induction emergent 45.1 to 45.8, canceled 60.5 to 63.3, noun-phrase completion emergent 26.0 to 26.9. Gains under 3 points per task. Still far below gold (NPC emergent gold 59.9).
limits: Gains are small in absolute terms; the gap to human and gold stays large. Judge and generator are from the same model family.
agent_relevance: A retrieve-then-filter step over associated concepts is a usable operator for blending, but expect small gains. Links to the semantic-network spreading-activation note in this series.

source: Song et al. (2025) Is a Peeled Apple Still Red? Evaluating LLMs' Ability for Conceptual Combination with Property Type (CCPT)
finding: LLM-as-judge for emergence agrees well with human ratings, so the metric is usable at scale.
numbers: Pearson 0.85, Spearman 0.83 on 300 pairs (3 MTurk raters each). Property-type annotation Fleiss kappa 0.59 (moderate).
limits: Agreement is for the relevance of a property to a concept, not for overall blend quality.
agent_relevance: A judge can score 'does concept X have property P' reliably enough to act as a check inside the loop.

source: Sato (2025) The Way We Prompt: Conceptual Blending, Neural Dynamics, and Prompt-Induced Transitions in LLMs
finding: Position paper mapping blending theory onto LLMs: input spaces = concepts in the prompt, generic space = pretraining knowledge and ontological constraints, blend = model output. Defines Prompt-Induced Transition (tone or meaning shift) and Prompt-Induced Hallucination (blending distant domains, e.g. periodic table with tarot gives coherent but ungrounded text). Proposes token and semantic entropy as signals.
numbers: No experiments or numbers in this paper.
limits: Conceptual mapping, not a test. The terms PIT and PIH are the author's own, cited mostly to his own preprints.
agent_relevance: The PIH idea is a warning: forced fusion of distant domains yields fluent but unfounded blends. Needs a grounding check.

source: Sato (2025) Waking Up an AI: A Quantitative Framework for Prompt-Induced Phase Transition in LLMs
finding: Controlled prompt test of whether LLMs respond differently to prompts that fuse two distant concepts (aperiodic tilings and traditional crafts) versus presenting them separately. Models can tell the two prompts apart when asked, but their affective response did not differ.
numbers: Responder: a custom GPT-4o persona. Judges: GPT-4o (3 responses x 5 judge runs = n=15 per prompt) and Gemini 2.5 Pro (1 response, n=5). Fused and non-fused prompts both beat the control (p < 0.05 or 0.01, one-tailed Welch t). Fused vs non-fused: no significant difference.
limits: Very small n. Outcome is an LLM-judged tone score, not blend quality. Gemini hit model-level limits on repeated evaluation. One author, one prompt pair, persona confound. n counts judge runs, not independent responses.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence that a 'fuse these' instruction alone changes little. Do not assume it adds integration; measure integration directly.
quote: current LLMs showed no significant difference in responsiveness between semantically fused and non-fused prompts

source: Olearo et al. (2025) Blending Concepts with Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
finding: Four zero-shot ways to blend concepts inside text-to-image diffusion (TEXTUAL embedding average, SWITCH prompt after t steps, ALTERNATE prompts per step, UNET layer-wise conditioning). No single method wins everywhere; results depend on prompt order, conceptual distance and seed.
numbers: User study: 100 participants ranking 4 methods over 22 concept pairs. Overall pairwise: ALTERNATE over SWITCH 51% (p=0.31, not significant); ALTERNATE over TEXTUAL 60%, SWITCH over TEXTUAL 61%, SWITCH over UNET 58%, ALTERNATE over UNET 57%, UNET over TEXTUAL 55% (all p<0.001).
limits: Categories differ and no two give the same preference order. In the 'Same class' category no method beat TEXTUAL. Seeds were tested qualitatively, not in the user study.
agent_relevance: Prompt order changes the blend for three of four methods (only TEXTUAL averaging is order-invariant). For an LLM agent: run both orders and several samples, then select.

source: Olearo et al. (2025) Blending Concepts with Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
finding: Blend outcome is asymmetric and seed-sensitive: swapping prompt order (lion/cat, eagle/peacock) shifts which concept dominates. Compound words ('rain bow') are order-sensitive too. UNET gave stable subtle blends across seeds; ALTERNATE sometimes produced no blend.
numbers: Ten random seeds per concept pair tested; blend-ratio sweeps shown for corgi/duck at 25/75, 50/50, 75/25.
limits: Qualitative, no effect sizes for the seed analysis.
agent_relevance: Sampling variance is a real factor: one blend sample is not evidence the model can blend. Use best-of-N with an external check.

source: Matsuhira et al. (2024) Investigating Conceptual Blending of a Diffusion Model for Improving Nonword-to-Image Generation (ACM MM 2024)
finding: First quantitative check of conceptual blending in Stable Diffusion. Interpolating the CLIP text embeddings of two concepts produces blended images mostly near the midpoint.
numbers: 1,000 noun pairs. At ratio 0.5: blended concept depiction (BCD, narrow) 62.1%, mixed concept depiction (MCD, broad) 86.2%. Averaged over all ratios: 0.389 and 0.471. Support 100-125 pairs per ratio.
limits: Detection uses CLIP-score classifiers, not humans. Authors note two blend types: co-occurring objects (calf in a cave) and texture or adjective blends (armoured spider). Co-photographed pairs mostly yield side-by-side, not true integration.
agent_relevance: Even 'blend' detection is split: showing both objects is not integration. A checker should separate juxtaposition from fusion.

source: Matsuhira et al. (2024) Investigating Conceptual Blending of a Diffusion Model for Improving Nonword-to-Image Generation (ACM MM 2024)
finding: Nonword-to-image generation: predicting a blended embedding for a nonword with kNN plus linear regression kept blending and image quality better than direct prediction.
numbers: Best setting (k=1000 per the text): BCD ratio up to 0.707 and MCD 0.789. kNN search over 26,143 training words; 1,000-noun evaluation set.
limits: FID-type quality metrics; a nonword task, not general blending. Exact baseline numbers not recorded.
agent_relevance: Blending as interpolation in embedding space needs the midpoint; edge ratios lose one concept.

source: Peng et al. (2025) Probing and Inducing Combinational Creativity in Vision-Language Models (CogSci 2025)
finding: CreativeMashup benchmark of 666 artist-made visual mashups with Identification, Explanation, Implication (IEI) annotations. Best VLMs beat average people at understanding blends but not experts.
numbers: Implication win rate: human experts 78.3, GPT-4o 73.5, GPT-4V 71.9, Gemini-1.5-Pro 71.7, Claude-3.5-Sonnet 62.9, average people 51.0, Claude-3-Opus 39.2, open LLaVA 20.1 to 40.6. Identification precision GPT-4o 75.67 vs people 53.42. Explanation precision GPT-4o 74.19, Claude-3.5-Sonnet 74.19, people 69.89. 11 models.
limits: Judge for implication is GPT-4o (85.1% and 81.6% consistent with two human experts on 200 comparisons). Human baseline from Prolific. Images are two-object mashups on plain backgrounds; narrow.
agent_relevance: Understanding a given blend is largely solved for frontier models; generating a good one is the weak step.

source: Peng et al. (2025) Probing and Inducing Combinational Creativity in Vision-Language Models (CogSci 2025)
finding: Prompt scaffold that raised generation quality: force the model to run the three IEI steps (identify the two inputs, explain shared attributes, derive implication) before writing the image prompt, compared with Identification+Implication only (II).
numbers: Friedman test p<0.0001 across Human Expert / II / IEI for all five image models; IEI beat II. Midjourney mean rank 1.98 (IEI) vs 2.40 (II). Midjourney win rate vs human expert 0.26 (II) to 0.35 (IEI). Stable Diffusion 3 barely improved.
limits: Artist images still ranked best overall. Sample size of raters not recovered from the text I read. Gain is largest when the image model is strong.
agent_relevance: Directly agent-usable: an explicit 'shared attributes' step between inputs and output helped. Caveat: the text step worked 90% of the time (36/40) but 27.8% (10/36) of good descriptions still failed to render, so execution was the bottleneck.

source: Wang, Petridis, Kwon, Ma, Chilton (2023) PopBlends: Strategies for Conceptual Blending with Large Language Models (CHI 2023)
finding: PopBlends: a GPT-3 pipeline for pop-culture and product blends. Stage 1: expand each domain into associations and find a connecting concept. Stage 2: expand the connector into scenes in each domain and insert one entity into the other's scene.
numbers: Stage 1 (connector relates to both domains): average accuracy 56.0% No-GPT, 55.3% Half-GPT, 58.7% Full-GPT (overall 56.7%); at least one good connector among five: 90.0%, 96.6%, 93.3% (overall 93.3%). 10 annotators. Stage 2: at least one related scene 98.3%; product scenes 89.1% (raw 80.0%), pop scenes 75.9% (raw 63.4%). GPT-3 entity-attribute accuracy averaged 2.86 of 5.
limits: 10 annotators. GPT-3 hallucinates attributes. Per-item accuracy is about half, so it works as generator plus filter.
agent_relevance: Concrete template of a blending operator in an LLM loop: expand, connect, expand, insert. Shows the value of generating many candidates and filtering.

source: Wang, Petridis, Kwon, Ma, Chilton (2023) PopBlends: Strategies for Conceptual Blending with Large Language Models (CHI 2023)
finding: User study: within-subjects, PopBlends vs general internet search. People produced more blend ideas and felt less load.
numbers: N=10 students (6 female, mean age 24.2). Ideas per pop-culture/product pair: 2.03 (SD 0.84) with PopBlends vs 0.87 (SD 0.56) with search; paired Wilcoxon p<0.001. Columbia summary: about double the blends at half the mental demand.
limits: N=10, six pairs each. Counts of ideas, not independent quality ratings. Authors' own system.
agent_relevance: LLM-generated connectors raise idea count for humans. For an agent, the connector list is the useful artifact.

source: Yang et al. (2025) Vibe Spaces for Creatively Connecting and Expressing Visual Concepts
finding: Vibe Blending: find the most relevant shared attributes between two images before blending. The paper reports that GPT Image 1 and Gemini 2.5 Flash Image blend by composing parts, transferring style or interpolating pixels rather than the shared 'vibe'. The proposed method is preferred most when the pair is hard to blend.
numbers: Human agreement on which method wins: 76.6% for Gemini vs theirs. Human consensus on which pair is harder to blend about 66%. Their difficulty score agrees with human difficulty 80.0%. Ten raters per comparison.
limits: Authors' own method wins. Table garbled in extraction; per-cell preference percentages not read reliably.
agent_relevance: Choosing which attribute to project is the key step, not the render. An explicit attribute-selection step matters, matching 'selective projection' in blending theory.

source: Yang et al. (2025) Vibe Spaces for Creatively Connecting and Expressing Visual Concepts
finding: An LLM judge of blend creativity only partly matches humans.
numbers: LLM top-1 agreement with the human most-preferred blend 35.7% on Totally Looks Like (chance 25%); top-2 match 55.1% and 51.8% on the two datasets. The LLM chose color or texture where humans chose hairstyle.
limits: Chance is 25% (four methods). Two image sets only.
agent_relevance: Do not trust an LLM judge as the only check on blend quality.
quote: humans are more consistent with one another, and the LLM captures a partial but meaningful overlap

source: Besold & Plaza (2015) Generalize and Blend: Concept Blending Based on Generalization, Analogy, and Amalgams (ICCC)
finding: COINVENT-style computational blending: generalise two inputs by anti-unification (HDTP), then combine with asymmetric amalgams. Worked examples: 'sign forest' (signpost and tree share a stem-like object fixed to the ground supporting something) and a foldable toothbrush (toothbrush plus pocketknife hinge and fold).
numbers: Two case studies, no quantitative evaluation. The shared generic space explains why 'forest of signs, spears, masts' works but 'forest of chairs' does not.
limits: Hand-written logical descriptions. Intermediate report. Blend evaluation is not implemented in the paper.
agent_relevance: A symbolic skeleton: find the shared generalisation, keep one input fixed, import selected parts. Can be written as a prompt template with code-checked consistency.

source: ACL 2026 poster, Evaluating Creative Generative AI with Conceptual Blending (Mark Turner site)
finding: Proposal to evaluate generative AI creativity as cross-domain conceptual integration. Uses FrameNet frames as input spaces and a rubric: completeness, clarity, relevance, understanding depth, coherence, execution time. Human-in-the-loop generation pipeline.
numbers: No numbers. Example blend: childbirth mapped onto financial investment.
limits: Poster only; no reliability or results reported. Authors invite shared annotation protocols and inter-rater tests.
agent_relevance: A ready rubric for scoring blend outputs; usable if reliability is tested first.

source: Eppe et al. (2018) A computational framework for conceptual blending, Artificial Intelligence 256:105-129
finding: COINVENT framework: generalisation of inputs as an answer set programming search, then blend creation and ranking by optimality principles.
numbers: Not read; PDF download failed.
limits: Seen only in search-result text.
agent_relevance: Same skeleton as the Besold-Plaza paper but with a solver and ranking by optimality principles.

source: Pereira (2007) Creativity and AI: A Conceptual Blending Approach (Divago)
finding: Divago: two input domains plus a generic space; blending principles applied iteratively until a stable solution is reached.
numbers: Not read; thesis not opened.
limits: Search snippet only.
agent_relevance: Oldest implemented blending search system; shows blending as iterated search with constraints.

source: Li, Zook, Davis, Riedl (2012) Goal-Driven Conceptual Blending: A Computational Approach for Creativity (ICCC)
finding: Goal-driven, context-sensitive blending to produce creative artifacts; cited by Besold and Plaza as a computational blending system.
numbers: Not opened; seen as a citation in an opened paper (the URL is that citing paper).
limits: Citation level only.
agent_relevance: A goal acts as a filter on blends: the blend must serve a purpose, which an agent can supply.

source: Mizrahi et al. (2026) structured recombination vs GPT-4o (ACL 2026)
finding: Search result states a structured recombination approach, judged by domain experts, beats GPT-4o on novelty and diversity.
numbers: Not opened; no numbers read.
limits: Search snippet only; may not be about blending theory.
agent_relevance: If confirmed, supports structured recombination over free prompting.

source: Chilton, Petridis, Agrawala (2019) VisiBlends: A flexible workflow for visual blends (CHI)
finding: Human-plus-computer workflow: user lists associated concepts, system retrieves images and matches shapes; the main precursor of PopBlends.
numbers: Not opened; cited in Ge & Parikh and PopBlends.
limits: Citation level only.
agent_relevance: Source of the 'expand associations, then find a connector' pattern.

source: BIG-bench conceptual combinations task (2023) and FakeReef (2024)
finding: Earlier benchmarks of emergent properties of combined concepts. The CCPT paper says they test emergent properties only, as multiple choice, with no generative task.
numbers: Sizes per the CCPT table: BIG-bench-CC 103 questions, FakeReef 854.
limits: Not opened; second-hand from the CCPT paper, which I did read.
agent_relevance: CCPT is the fuller test; these are older, narrower baselines.
